title: Nightly snapshot records one row per then-open job per tab per calendar date
permissions_required: Backend/database (or dev-support) access to inspect the stored WIP snapshot rows — this is a backend capture behavior that runs without a signed-in user.
preconditions: 1. Open work orders exist across the organization on the capture date.
2. You can inspect the stored snapshot rows after the nightly capture runs (arrange the verification route with the developers).

3. To see the information this test asks for you need the browser's own developer tools: press F12 (or Ctrl+Shift+I; on a Mac Cmd+Option+I) and open the "Network" tab, then reload the page. There is nothing to install — it is built into Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Where a check also asks you to confirm what is stored on the server, ask a developer to read it back for you — that part cannot be seen from the browser.
steps: 1. Note the set of open work orders before the nightly capture runs.
2. After the capture, inspect the stored snapshot rows for that calendar date.
3. Let the capture run again the next day and inspect again.
4. If a manual re-run of the capture is available, re-run it for the same date and inspect that date's rows again.
expected:
1. Once per day the system records one row per then-open work order per tab — a work order whose approved lines fall in more than one tab is captured as one row for each matching tab, each row holding only that tab's share of the money, so the saved history reconciles with the on-screen tabs. Rows are keyed by work order, tab, and calendar date.
2. The next day's capture adds the same per-work-order-per-tab rows under the new date; a work order open on both days has its rows for each date. A work order can have more than one row on the same date (one row for each tab it appears in), but never two rows for the same work order, tab and date together.
3. Re-running the capture for the SAME date replaces that date's rows — the day's existing rows are removed and re-recorded from current data, never duplicated.
4. Each snapshot row captures, at minimum: the work order, the tab (line-state bucket) the row represents, its status, that tab's Earned value, that tab's Remaining value, the location and organization (copied from the work order), and the snapshot's calendar date.

Note for the tester: you cannot check this one from any screen. These figures are written each night by a background process, and nothing in the report reads them back in this version. If you cannot see the figures anywhere, mark this test BLOCKED - do not mark it failed, and do not raise it as a problem.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8582 and story SV-8667 (WIP Story 11), both read on 18 August 2026, and the Work In Progress report specification version 22 (S11-R1, S11-R2), read on 18 August 2026, and as per Chris Ward's answer of 18 August 2026 (the nightly snapshot is recorded one row per work order per tab per day), recorded in his answer in this file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bilalmuzamil-sketch/Manual-test-Cases/claude/slack-session-0sxnd9/build/report-suite/chris-answers-2026-08-18/chris-answer-snapshot-grain-2026-08-18.txt.
This differs from the older wording in the same specification (Story 11, S11-R1 at version 21), which recorded one row per then-open work order per calendar date, with no per-tab split. Chris Ward confirmed on 18 August 2026 that the grain is one row per work order per tab per day, now recorded in specification version 22, so that newest source is followed here.
Last checked against build v3.5-f77875c on 8/6/2026.
